runs.title: Checkout - Teaser
runs.logline: During a hurricane evacuation, a night concierge sees the same unknown woman on every security monitor — then every elevator opens onto black ocean water.

preview.title: CHECKOUT
preview.prompt_text:
Create a 12-second cinematic teaser for "CHECKOUT," a supernatural prestige thriller — hurricane luxury hotel, sodium emergency lighting, drowned-teal shadows, chrome rain on glass. Pacing: brutal 0.3–0.5s cuts tightening to 0.2s flash-frames at the drop. Needle-drop: low sub-bass pulse, distant generator thrum, one dead-silence beat before title.

[0:00–0:03 — Monitors]
Handheld whip through empty marble lobby, four security monitors flicker — the same pale woman in lobby, pool, corridor, rooftop at once. Hard cut: young concierge breath fogging the glass, reflection wrong by half a beat.

[0:03–0:07 — Evacuation]
Rapid-fire: guests in wet couture sprinting, PA distortion, palm fronds hammering windows. Flash-frames: room key, wristband, elevator indicator, ocean on a floor map that should read 12.

[0:07–0:11 — Flood]
Power snap. Every elevator door slides open to roaring black water instead of a floor. Concierge stares into the shaft — her face duplicated on a monitor behind her, smiling.

[0:11–0:12 — Title]
Vacuum silence. Whisper: "you're still checked in." CHECKOUT slams in chrome serif. Subsonic hit. Black.

Style: Anamorphic 2.39:1, halation on practicals, crushed blacks, magenta-cyan split-tone, Alexa grain. Faces lit from below. No logos. Blackout on final hit.

runs.title: The Last Prescription
runs.logline: When a bored high-school graduate forced into a nursing-home job learns from a dying resident that the facility controls a hidden drug trade documented in a locked diary, he must find the courage to expose the business or claim the dead man's connections after an unexpected death leaves the empire leaderless.

preview.title: The Last Prescription
preview.prompt_text:
Text-only 16:9 cinematic live-action teaser, grounded contemporary crime drama, realistic performances, restrained suspense, humid small-town atmosphere, muted institutional greens and faded beige contrasted with deep amber practical light, subtle handheld camera, natural skin texture, no glamour, no exaggerated action, coherent recurring characters: MARCUS REID, an 18-year-old bored high-school graduate with messy dark hair, gray work polo, and plastic name tag; OSCAR HENDRICKS, an elderly resident with silver hair, intelligent eyes, oxygen tubing, and a faded cardigan.
0:00-0:02 — slow tracking shot through a quiet nursing-home medication corridor at dusk; Marcus pushes a metal cart past closed doors as fluorescent lights buzz, pill bottles rattle, and distant televisions murmur.
0:02-0:04 — hard cut to Oscar's room; intimate close-up as Oscar slides a small brass key across the table toward Marcus and whispers, "Everything is written down," while a locked black diary sits beneath his hand.
0:04-0:06 — rapid but realistic inserts: Marcus discreetly removes several prescription bottles from a delivery bag, hides them inside his jacket, and looks at his reflection in a dark medication-room window; low bass pulse begins.
0:06-0:07 — hard cut to morning; Marcus opens Oscar's door and freezes beside the bed, sunlight slicing across Oscar's still face; all sound drops into one beat of complete silence.
0:07-0:09 — close-up of Marcus unlocking the diary; pages reveal handwritten names, addresses, dosage codes, and a crude map of the town as footsteps approach outside the room.
0:09-0:11 — handheld push-in as Marcus looks through the doorway toward several silent residents watching him from the corridor; one elderly woman slowly closes the medication room blinds.
0:11-0:12 — hard cut to black, then a sharp amber title hit: THE LAST PRESCRIPTION; beneath it, the sound of the diary snapping shut and Marcus's terrified whisper, "What did you leave me?" No subtitles, no logos, no disconnected shots, no fantasy elements, no graphic violence.
